skill.name: agent-mail
skill.description: Coordinates multiple coding agents through an MCP mail server with identities, threaded messages, file reservations, contact policies, and audit-friendly exports.
skill.summary: Coordinate coding agents with shared mail, reservations, contact rules, and searchable project history.
skill.author: Dicklesworthstone

security_audit.summary: Most static backtick findings are false positives caused by Markdown formatting, not executable Ruby or shell backticks. Confirmed risks remain around the remote pipe-to-shell installer, hidden local mailbox storage, signing-key handling, broad Docker network binding, and documented control bypasses.

remediation.issue: Remote installer is piped directly to bash.
remediation.suggestion: Replace curl-pipe-bash installation with a pinned release, package manager command, or checksum-verified script that users inspect before execution.

remediation.issue: Human Overseer messages bypass contact policies.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit authorization, audit logging, and opt-in configuration before allowing policy bypass or priority-changing agent instructions.

remediation.issue: Mailbox state is stored in a hidden home directory by default.
remediation.suggestion: Document retention, permissions, and cleanup clearly, and allow users to choose a visible storage root for sensitive projects.

remediation.issue: Signing-key path is used in export instructions.
remediation.suggestion: Document key file permissions, avoid committing keys, and recommend short-lived or project-specific signing keys.

remediation.issue: Docker example binds the HTTP service to all interfaces.
remediation.suggestion: Default examples should bind to localhost unless deployment uses TLS, authentication, and firewall controls.

remediation.issue: Pre-commit guard can be bypassed with an environment variable.
remediation.suggestion: Treat bypass as an audited emergency action and require a written reason in shared repositories.

content.user_title: Coordinate Coding Agents with Agent Mail
content.value_statement: Parallel coding agents can overwrite work or miss important context. Agent Mail gives them shared identities, inboxes, file reservations, and searchable coordination history.
actual_capabilities: Registers memorable agent identities for each project workspace.
Sends and receives threaded messages with importance levels and acknowledgments.
Creates advisory file reservations with conflict reporting and lease renewal.
Supports contact policies for open, automatic, contacts-only, or blocked messaging.
Provides searchable message history and read-only mailbox exports.
Includes a pre-commit guard that checks exclusive file reservations.
limitations: Requires a running Agent Mail server and compatible MCP client configuration.
File reservations are advisory and do not replace source control conflict handling.
Security depends on bearer token handling, storage permissions, and network exposure.
Some export and recovery workflows require local command-line tools.

use_cases.title: Coordinate parallel code changes
use_cases.description: Reserve files, announce work, and exchange status updates between agents working in one repository.
use_cases.target_user: Engineering teams using several coding agents

use_cases.title: Track agent communication history
use_cases.description: Search project messages, summarize threads, and review decisions across long-running development sessions.

use_cases.title: Share audited project mailboxes
use_cases.description: Export read-only coordination records for stakeholders, archives, or post-project review.

prompt_templates.title: Start a coordinated session
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for one agent joining a project.
prompt_templates.prompt: Start an Agent Mail session for this project. Register my agent identity, fetch my inbox, and summarize any urgent messages.

prompt_templates.title: Reserve files before work
prompt_templates.scenario: Basic coordination before editing shared files.
prompt_templates.prompt: Reserve the files I plan to edit, report any conflicts, and draft a short message announcing the work to related agents.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a thread update
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate workflow for keeping collaborators informed.
prompt_templates.prompt: Find the thread for this task, summarize recent updates, and prepare a concise progress reply with blockers and next steps.

prompt_templates.title: Audit multi-agent activity
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review after several agents worked in parallel.
prompt_templates.prompt: Search the mailbox for this release, identify unresolved coordination risks, summarize file reservation conflicts, and recommend follow-up actions.

output_examples.input: Start a new session and check whether anyone needs my attention.
output_examples.output: Agent identity registered. Inbox contains two normal updates and one urgent request about the authentication module. No file reservations are active for this agent.

output_examples.input: Reserve the authentication files and tell the frontend agent what I am changing.
output_examples.output: Reservation requested for the authentication paths. One overlapping reservation was found, so the message asks the frontend agent to confirm the API contract before edits continue.

output_examples.input: Summarize coordination history for the release manager.
output_examples.output: The summary lists completed tasks, unresolved blockers, agents involved, and the threads that need human review before release.

best_practices: Start each agent session by registering identity and checking the inbox.
Reserve files before editing and release reservations when work is complete.
Use task identifiers consistently in subjects, threads, reservations, and commits.
anti_patterns: Do not treat advisory reservations as a replacement for git review and tests.
Do not expose the HTTP server without strong token handling and network controls.
Do not bypass the pre-commit guard except for documented emergency recovery.

faq.question: What does Agent Mail add to a coding agent workflow?
faq.answer: It gives agents shared messaging, identities, file reservations, contact controls, and searchable coordination history.

faq.question: Does it prevent all edit conflicts?
faq.answer: No. Reservations signal intent and help coordination, but git review and tests remain necessary.

faq.question: Can humans message agents through it?
faq.answer: Yes. The web interface includes Human Overseer messaging for high-priority human-to-agent communication.

faq.question: Where does it store mailbox data?
faq.answer: The documented default storage root is a hidden directory in the user home folder.

faq.question: Does it support read-only exports?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents static mailbox exports with optional signing, encryption, and scrubbing presets.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code compatible workflows.
